entry.sum: The depth of a finitely generated module $M$ over a Noetherian local ring is the length of a longest $M$-regular sequence in the maximal ideal, equivalently the first $i$ with $\mathrm{Ext}^i(k,M)\neq0$; it never exceeds $\dim M$. $M$ is Cohen-Macaulay when $\operatorname{depth}M = \dim M$, equivalently when every system of parameters is a regular sequence, and maximal Cohen-Macaulay when its depth equals $\dim R$.
entry.why: Cohen-Macaulay rings are the setting in which intersection theory, duality and the unmixedness theorem take their simplest form, and hypotheses such as 'maximal Cohen-Macaulay', '$(S_2)$' or 'depth at least $2$' appear throughout commutative algebra, algebraic geometry and combinatorial commutative algebra.

links.note: A simplicial complex is called Cohen-Macaulay when its Stanley-Reisner ring is; Reisner's criterion turns this into vanishing of link homology, and Stanley used it to prove the upper bound conjecture for simplicial spheres.
Maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules over a Gorenstein ring form a Frobenius category whose stable category is the singularity category; over a hypersurface they are matrix factorizations.
Guan and Hu formalised depth (via Ext), the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula, Cohen-Macaulay rings and the Auslander-Buchsbaum-Serre criterion in Lean 4.
